TS-PP-002.how: The prescribed fix is declined on all three counts, with two adjacent real defects fixed as a by-product. (1) lib/state/index.js is not a facade for the folder, so lib/server.js is not bypassing one. Its own JSDoc states its job: 'Gather everything the router needs, concurrently and with a hard ceiling.' It exports four aggregation functions (invalidate, readingSnapshot, todoSnapshot, snapshot) and has never re-exported a sibling's surface. Nine other modules import lib/state/*.js siblings directly (lib/engine.js, lib/reclaim.js, lib/reader.js, lib/companions-control.js, lib/actuators/index.js, lib/doctor.js at five imports, bin/interstice.js, and six test files), so the siblings are entry points in their own right, not internals of index.js. Turning it into a barrel would leave lib/server.js the only consumer using the barrel, and would make lib/engine.js, which imports index.js on the router's hot path, load lib/state/companions.js and the companion control graph it never touches. (2) lib/focus/breakers/display.js is not an implementation folder being reached into. `screenLocked` is a documented public export with its own JSDoc, lib/focus has no index.js entry module, and each of the three breakers is separately exported and separately tested (test/focus-breaker-display.test.js, -frontmost, -video). lib/focus/tracker.js consumes only `createDisplayBreaker`; doctor deliberately wants the raw probe, so routing it through tracker would mean inventing an entry module to re-export one function used once. (3) The route handlers are not reading internals. `daemon.reader.signingIn` is a getter carrying its own JSDoc contract ('True while a sign-in window owns the profile...'), and `signInStatus()` is already called on the line beside it. `daemon.reader.seq` is a plain published field that reader.state() also returns; adding a method that wraps it would be a second name for one number. FIXED as a by-product: lib/doctor.js's frontmost check did `const { frontmostApp } = await import('./state/system.js')` while the same file already imports frontmostApp statically on line 8, so the dynamic import was a redundant second load shadowing a static one; it is removed. And the one field read that did have an existing contract, `if (!daemon.engine.gap)` in POST /debug/rung, now reads `daemon.engine.status.open`, which the Engine's `get status()` already publishes as `open: Boolean(this.gap)`, so no new API was added.

RN-ASYNC-PARALLEL.how: Both sites now start their two independent operations together. lib/doctor.js's reading-rung check runs `const [portFree, sessionCarried] = await Promise.all([portIsFree(readerPort), hasAmazonSession(...)])`: a bind attempt against the reader port and a read of the cookie store share no input, and doctor is a command somebody sits and watches. lib/server.js's POST /api/reading/view runs `const [body, state] = await Promise.all([readBody(req), readingSnapshot(config)])`: draining the request body waits on the panel's socket, the snapshot waits on the Kindle store, `readingSnapshot` takes only `config`, and the panel calls this route on every poll while the book is on screen. readBody stays the first element, so its 'data' and 'end' listeners are attached synchronously when Promise.all evaluates the array, before anything can yield; no chunk can be missed. Error semantics are unchanged in both cases: the enclosing `check(...)` and the route's own handler already caught whichever error arrived first.

RN-ASYNC-DEPENDENCIES.how: The three awaits in lib/state/anki.js `reconnect` are not independent, so the promise-first form the rule prescribes would introduce a race rather than remove a waterfall. `disableAppNap(ANKI_BUNDLE_IDS)` is not a query: lib/state/system.js:241-255 shows it runs `/usr/bin/defaults write <bundleId> NSAppSleepDisabled -bool YES`. Cocoa reads NSAppSleepDisabled out of the application's defaults domain when the process starts. The prescribed shape starts `launchedP = runP.then(r => (r ? false : launchHeadless('Anki')))` without waiting on `nappedP`, so the copy of Anki this function itself launches can start before the preference write has landed, and that instance is still subject to App Nap. That is precisely the failure the whole reconnect path exists to prevent, and it is the failure lib/doctor.js's preflight block names first: 'macOS App Nap suspends Anki when it is backgrounded, which is exactly its state when we query it, and AnkiConnect then stops answering. Symptom: nothing happens, no error anywhere.' The dependency is real; it runs through the macOS defaults database rather than through a JavaScript value, which is why static analysis cannot see it. No reordering was made. A six-line comment was added at the site stating that the ordering is load-bearing and why, so the next audit does not re-open it.

RN-SERVER-HOIST-STATIC-IO.how: lib/server.js serveFile now keeps each shipped page in memory and re-reads it only when the file on disk has moved. The per-request existsSync plus readFileSync became one statSync, with the cached entry used when both mtimeMs and size match, and a readFileSync only on a miss; the statSync failing is what produces the 404 now, so the missing-file branch is preserved. Size is checked alongside mtime because two edits inside one clock tick are unlikely rather than impossible, and a stale panel is the one bug this cache must not introduce. Deliberately not a plain module-level read: assetStamp() and the panel's self-reload are built on an edit to web/panel.html reaching an already-open window, and a cache with no expiry is a slower way of not shipping the change. Deliberately scoped to the server closure rather than the module, because what is stored is the page with this daemon's control token already injected by injectToken(); a module-level cache would hand a second createServer in the same process the first one's token, and the tests do stand up servers in-process. Injection happens on the read path, so every served page still carries its own daemon's token. A read counter is exposed through the existing stats() as `assetReads`, so the cache working is something the operator can look at in /api/health rather than something they are told.
RN-SERVER-HOIST-STATIC-IO.verified: Both halves proven against the live daemon on port 7420 after restarting it onto this code.
